title: BLS12-381 G1: Cheon attack with fixed-base comb and sequential precomputation accounting

claims.statement: For the protected BLS12-381 G1 target T=[s]P0 with the supplied powers A_i=[s^i]P0, i=1..n, at the protected scoring n=2^20, the deterministic two-phase Cheon attack specified in proof.md recovers the uniform secret s in 1..r-1 with success probability 1. It uses only A_1=T and A_d for d=2^20, which divides r-1 and is supplied at the scoring n as the protected rules state. Phase 1 solves k0 in [0,M), M=(r-1)/d, by baby-step giant-step in [zeta_hat^k0]P0; phase 2 computes the runtime point S=[zeta^(-k0)]T and solves k1 in [0,d); s=zeta^(k0)*zeta_check^(k1) mod r is verified by [s]P0=T. Scalar multiplication uses the verified production GLV pair (beta,lambda) and fixed-base comb tables with w=16: each 127-bit GLV half needs at most 8 table-point additions, so the online phase is 17 additions and no doublings. The six comb tables serve A_d, phi(A_d), P0, phi(P0), and the runtime S and phi(S); each has 8 blocks of 2^16 entries. The online ledger charges 33 reference additions (1 unit each), 33 random table lookups (2 units each) and 16 units of itemised overhead, i.e. E=115 units per scalar multiplication. The comb precomputation is sequential and dependent, with a standalone Fermat inversion per point operation: 6*(8*65535+112)=3,146,352 point operations, each bounded by 640 F_p multiplications (245,120 instructions) plus the 6M/7M formula and 3,000 instructions for additions, reductions and control, i.e. at most 250,801 instructions per operation and 2^39.52 instructions (2^28.53 units) in total; the ledger charges PRECOMB=2^31 units, over five times that bound, included in preprocessing and in the total and not amortised over future targets. Online additions are independent and batched over B=2^64 live chains with the 240-byte-per-chain workspace counted; the baby table is a sorted array of m records (96-byte point and 16-byte index, since 118 index bits are needed), merge sort is charged 5 units per entry over 118 passes and binary search 4 units per giant lookup, with no hashing assumptions. The total is at most 2^125.329412 target-group-operation equivalents, i.e. the exact score 31332353/250000 = 125.329412. Peak memory is at most 2^126 bytes (ledger 2^125.2358996), preprocessing at most 2^124.336 units (ledger 2^124.3354353) and included, and nonuniform advice is zero bytes. The success probability is exact and unconditional; the cost is analytic under the protected accounting conventions. No production-size execution and no novelty are claimed.

experiments.purpose: Recompute the exact production ledger and assert the declared rounded score; verify the r-1 factorisation, generator 7, order of zeta_hat, production GLV pair and [r]P0=O on the protected curve, the 130-bit decomposition bound, the six comb tables and the sequential precomputation bound; run a comb self-test and complete two-phase Cheon recoveries using the comb (including a runtime S table) on a small elliptic curve and a small prime-order group. Toy runs are evidence at their actual scope only and do not establish a production success probability or production cost.
